newsitem.title: USA: Verdict against CB Commercial Upheld.
newsitem.headline: Verdict against CB Commercial Upheld.

text.p: A New Jersey judge Thursday upheld a $7.1 million sex discrimination jury verdict against CB Commercial Real Estate Services Group Inc., lawyers for the plaintiff said.
The November 1996 verdict was comprised of $1.5 million in compensatory damages and $5 million in punitive damages. The judge also awarded $638,399 in legal fees.
Bruce Atkins, the plaintiff's attorney, said he believed this to be one of the largest total damage amounts ever awarded in a sex discrimination case.
In Thursday's ruling, Superior Court Judge James Murphy denied a motion by CB Commercial to set the verdict aside.

The plaintiff, Martha Mogull, who had been the first female vice president at the firm, alleged that CB Commercial senior managers removed her from accounts she had helped to build and gave them to male brokers. She also alleged that senior managers gave better real estate deals to male employees to handle.
Mogull, who had worked at the firm for over 12 years, was fired in 1992 for what the company said was poor productivity. Mogull said that she was one of the top producers in the Hackensack office.
